studies.title: Only This Was Asked
studies.meaning: The sentence is restrictive: they were commanded with nothing except this. What follows is short enough to be a definition. Worship directed to God with the religion made purely His, uprightness of the kind associated with Abraham, and then two practices. The classical commentators note that the whole content of what earlier communities were given is summarised here in one line, and the closing phrase calls it the upright way.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan, in a short surah about the People of the Scripture and the idolaters and the clear evidence that came to them. The ayah before it says the earlier communities split only after that evidence arrived. So this line arrives as a summary of what was always asked, addressed to an audience in Medina that included communities with long scriptural traditions of their own.

keyTerms.note: From a verb meaning to clear something of what is mixed into it, used of refining metal and of milk separated from what floats on it. Sincerity is described as removal rather than as addition.
A plural for people who turn from something crooked toward what is straight. The word is used of Abraham repeatedly, so it carries a specific figure with it rather than a general disposition.
From the root for standing and for setting something right. Calling a way of life upright uses a builder's word: what is described is a thing that does not lean, rather than a thing that is true.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Medina held communities that had been arguing about scripture for generations, and the newcomers from Mecca arrived into that conversation. Religious identity there was inherited and detailed, expressed in calendars, diets and long-standing disagreements. An ayah that reduces what was ever asked to one sentence would have landed on people who could recite far longer lists.
studies.didYouKnow: The classical collections preserve a report that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) told one of his companions by name that God had commanded him to recite this surah to him, and that the man wept and asked whether he had been mentioned. It is one of the very few surahs attached to an individual listener in that way.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The ayah makes continuity the claim. What is asked here is described as what was always asked, so the differences between communities are located in what was added afterwards rather than in the original instruction. It also puts direction before content: the first requirement is not an act but the orientation of an act, which means two people doing the same thing may not be doing the same thing.

crossReferences.why: Repeats the same phrase about purity of direction and then describes people who add intermediaries to it.
Attaches the same word for uprightness to Abraham, which is where its associations come from.
States the same continuity across all messengers, reducing what was sent to one sentence.

studies.applyIt: Pick one thing you do regularly for God and ask what else is in it: habit, appearance, the approval of a particular person. Do not try to remove those. Just name them once, honestly. The word this ayah uses for sincerity means clearing something of what is mixed in, and you cannot clear what you have not identified.
